packageRules.description: Automerge everything that is not a major. The gate is make check, which CI runs as one job and branch protection requires; a bump that breaks anything cannot reach main, and a bump that breaks nothing does not need a human to look at it.
A major is a changelog to read, not a number to bump.
flake.lock is not automerged: nothing in CI opens the flake, so a nixpkgs bump that renames or drops go_1_26 would land on a green make check that never looked. A human reads this one.
One pull request for the Go module set rather than five, since x/ tags together.
The Makefile's tool pins, grouped: they are one toolchain and make check is one gate over all of them.

Go itself is pinned to 1.26 deliberately — golang/go#80974 makes 1.27 miscount statements, which is the one bug a coverage tool cannot ship on. CL 819000 fixed it for 1.28 with no 1.27 backport, so this lifts when 1.28 ships and not before. One name, because `go` is what both the gomod and github-actions managers emit — flake.nix's pin is a nixpkgs attribute no manager reads, so unblocking means editing it, go.mod and the workflow by hand. The constraints block above stops an ordinary bump raising the directive past this.

customManagers.description: Tool versions that live outside go.mod: the Makefile's *_VERSION pins, fetched with `go run pkg@version`, and .custom-gcl.yml's two, which decide what binary `make lint` builds. Both files are matched, because golangci-lint is pinned in both and only the .custom-gcl.yml one governs the lint gate — bumping the Makefile alone would leave the gate on the old version with make check green.

nix.description: flake.lock's nixpkgs input. The devShell is the only thing the flake builds, so this moves the contributor toolchain and nothing a user installs.

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix does not wait for Monday.
